recent_performance_reflections.no_new_lesson: This is ordinary variance around the prior harvest rule: after a material USDCAD win, three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse is the known harvest trigger. The original process remains sound if winner size is now cut and only a residual rate stub is kept.
recent_performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: The book treated the SOFR/CORRA and US2/CA2 gap as sufficient to hold winner-size long USDCAD after a material run. Observed path was a large giveback with spot now 1.3995 through the 1.401 entry, while three-digit oil, rising Canadian impulse, and a Bank of Canada hike poll supported CAD. That is harvest-trigger tape, not a dip that validates winner size.

recent_performance_reflections.no_new_lesson: No new lesson: further giveback after the first harvest cut is ordinary variance around a still-green residual. The prior process remains sound — oil plus a rising Canadian impulse is a harvest trigger, and leftover United States rate edge belongs in reduced size rather than winner size.
recent_performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: Expected the US-CA rate gap to keep a USD/CAD long valid and expected three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse to force harvest rather than peak-size hold. That harvest ran (20m to 15m). Giveback of about 80 percent of MFE on the residual was larger than a clean hold-the-reduced-book path; WTI at 97.15 is friendlier to remaining USD/CAD edge than the prior three-digit oil regime, but it did not arrive as a full offset to rising prima and CAD hike pricing. Peak open profit was not a level the 15m book was entitled to keep.

The expected path was a grind higher in dollar-Canada while United States yields stayed restrictive versus Canada. The realized path was an overshoot to a large peak, then a giveback as oil held above 100 and Canada's relative impulse improved. Residual profit is still positive versus entry but far below the maximum favorable excursion, which is a harvest failure rather than a thesis reversal on the dollar leg.
